sentiment.rationale: The document reports a 6% revenue increase and 22% NII growth, but forward guidance is not explicitly raised; management expresses confidence in being 'well-positioned' but also acknowledges 'economic uncertainty' and a 'weakened capital markets environment.' The net reserve release was minimal ($48M vs $2.2B a year ago), and the provision for credit losses increased significantly, reflecting a dampening macroeconomic outlook. The score is slightly positive due to strong organic loan growth and operating leverage, but tempered by cautious forward language and lack of a formal guidance raise.

summary.revenue: Total revenue, net of interest expense, increased 6% to $22.7 billion. Net interest income (NII) increased 22% to $12.4 billion. Noninterest income declined 9% to $10.2 billion.
summary.eps: Diluted earnings per share of $0.73, down from $1.03 in Q2-21.
summary.guidance: Not disclosed. No explicit forward guidance on revenue, earnings, or growth was provided. Management stated: 'As we enter the second half of the year, we believe we are well-positioned to deliver for our shareholders while continuing to invest in our people, businesses and communities.'
summary.margin: Net interest yield (FTE) was 1.86%, up 17 bps from Q1-22. Efficiency ratio was 67% for Q2-22, compared to 70% in Q2-21. Pretax margin for GWIM improved to 28% from 26%.
key_risks: Provision for credit losses increased $2.1 billion to $523 million, reflecting a dampening macroeconomic outlook and loan growth.
Noninterest income declined 9% to $10.2 billion, primarily reflecting weaker capital markets.
Noninterest expense included approximately $425 million recognized for certain regulatory matters.
Total investment banking fees (excl. self-led) decreased 47% to $1.1 billion, reflecting weaker industry-wide underwriting activity.
Global Banking revenue decreased 2%, driven by lower investment banking fees and mark-to-market losses related to leveraged finance positions.
Consumer net charge-offs increased $185 million from Q1-22, including $85 million from non-core mortgage sales.
key_opportunities: Net interest income up 22% to $12.4 billion, driven by higher interest rates, lower premium amortization and loan growth.
Average loan and lease balances up 12% to $1.0 trillion, led by strong commercial loan growth and higher consumer balances.
Fourth consecutive quarter of operating leverage (418 bps in Q2-22).
Consumer Banking added ~241,000 net new Consumer checking accounts in Q2-22; record 35.1 million Consumer checking accounts.
Global Wealth and Investment Management added more than 5,100 net new relationships across Merrill and Private Bank.
Sales and trading revenue up 17% to $4.2 billion, including FICC up 19% (excl. DVA).
Global Transaction Services revenue up 32% to $2.4 billion.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Brian Moynihan stated: 'Our strong organic growth engine once again was evident... we believe we are well-positioned to deliver for our shareholders while continuing to invest in our people, businesses and communities.'
